chunks: From him, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Al-Hajjal, from Hafs ibn Abu A'isha, who said:

Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) sent one of his servants on an errand, but he was delayed. So Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) went out after him because of his delay, and found him sleeping. He sat by his head, soothing him, until he woke up. When he woke up, Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said to him: 'O so-and-so, by Allah, that is not for you. You sleep during the night and the day, but the day is for us from you.'
ai.seo_question: What is the Islamic perspective on work hours and the rights of servants in Shia tradition?
ai.summary: In this narration from *Al-Kafi*, Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) demonstrates a nuanced approach to labor rights by distinguishing between the servant's personal time and their professional obligations. By finding the servant sleeping during work hours and gently rebuking him, the Imam highlights that while the night is for the servant's rest, the day is dedicated to fulfilling the master's needs, thereby establishing a clear ethical framework for employer-employee relations in Shia jurisprudence.

en.hubeali: H 14498 – From him, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Al-Hajjaal, from Hafs Bin Abu A’isha who said:

‘Abu Abdullahasws sent one of hisasws servants on an errand. He was delayed. So Abu Abdullahasws went out to see why he had been delayed. Heasws found him sleeping. So heasws sat near to his head and caressed it (and waited) until he woke up. So when he was awake, Abu Abdullahasws said to him: ‘O so and so, by Allahazwj, that is not for you. The night is for you to sleep in and the day from you is for usasws’.
en.sarwar: 50. From him, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Al-Hajjaal, from Hafs Bin Abu A’isha who said:

‘Abu Abdullah (a.s.) sent one of his (a.s.) servants on an errand. He was delayed. So Abu Abdullah (a.s.) went out to see why he had been delayed. He (a.s.) found him sleeping. So he (a.s.) sat near to his head and caressed it (and waited) until he woke up. So when he was awake, Abu Abdullah (a.s.) said to him: ‘O so and so, by Allah (azwj), that is not for you. The night is for you to sleep in and the day from you is for us (a.s.)’.
